# Fixed-box all-mass polynomial readouts: coefficient field, degree, and number

Status: LOCAL FROZEN AUTHOR WORKING / UNREVIEWED. RESULT_ONLY / COMPOSE candidate in the existing readout family. This is one complete author argument with its context; no independent review, Source publication, research checkpoint, Native execution, or new Tool/paper is claimed.

## 1. Question, exact category, and quantifiers

Keep the actual seven full coset readouts on the known chart c + Z^6: the six coordinate directions e_1,...,e_6 and v = (1,...,1). Write their joint map as O. A full coset readout means the sum on every coset of the corresponding integer line; it is not a selected collection of bins.

Keep exactly the single-long-axis box

B = {0,1,2,3} x {0,1,2}^5.

The states are all functions f : B -> N_0, extended by zero outside c + B. Their populations have no common upper bound. The original seven readouts include the total population through their bin sums, so equality of O already gives equality of mass.

Let K be a specified subfield of R, with the usual characteristic-zero embedding. Choose a finite family P_1,...,P_r in K[u_1,...,u_6], once and for all, before the mass and the states are supplied. Define

T_P(f) = sum_(u in B) f(c+u) P(u) in K.                                      (1)

Each added output is one exact element of K. In particular, an R-valued output is an abstract exact real value, not a floating-point sample or a noise-tolerant measurement. An element of Q(sqrt(2)) generally carries two rational coordinates; calling it one field-valued output does not make those coordinates cost-free.

The property being tested is

for every f,g in N_0^B:
    O(f) = O(g) and T_(P_i)(f) = T_(P_i)(g) for every i
    imply f = g.                                                           (2)

Equivalently, the same fixed family must distinguish every fiber at every mass. Families allowed to depend on a previously bounded mass are a different problem. The degree of a nonempty family means the maximum total degree of its members. Outputs nonlinear in f, arbitrary lookup functions, moving boxes, other boxes, added Native axes, and noisy recovery are outside this category.

This is a new consumer of the exact boxed integer kernel. The earlier mass63 minimum-degree-seven theorem alone does not establish (2).

## 2. Two existing whole inputs and the finite pairing

Use the polynomial notation X^u for the chart index u, and set x = X_1 and

G(X) = (X^v - 1) product_(j=1)^6 (X_j - 1).

The accepted boxed whole proves, for any signed integer array h supported in B,

O(h) = 0  iff  H_h(X) = G(X)(a + b x), with unique a,b in Z.                 (3)

Conversely, every pair a,b in Z gives a signed array supported in this actual B. This is an integer statement, not merely a two-dimensional real nullspace.

The same whole gives the positive and negative mass of this difference:

mu(a,b) = 32(|a|+|b|) + 31|a-b|.                                           (4)

In particular mu is positive for (a,b) != (0,0), and its minimum is 63. A difference h in (3) has zero total mass. Therefore h_+ and h_- are actual nonnegative states in B of the same mass mu(a,b), with equal original readouts. They may be used as collision witnesses; an arbitrary real kernel vector would not suffice.

For any states f,g with difference h, pointwise positivity gives f >= h_+ and g >= h_-. Their common mass is therefore at least mu(a,b). Conversely every integer mass at least mu(a,b) is attained by adding the same nonnegative population at a fixed voxel to h_+,h_-. This proves the mass-threshold quantifiers used below.

For a finite polynomial H = sum h_u X^u, use the literal finite pairing

<P,H> = sum h_u P(u).

If Delta_w P(q) = P(q+w)-P(q), multiplication by X^w-1 on H is adjoint in this pairing to Delta_w on P. Thus the moment whole's finite identity, also obtained directly by expanding the seven factors, is

<P, X^p G> = D P(p),
D = Delta_v Delta_(e_1)...Delta_(e_6).                                      (5)

All these are finite sums on the original chart. No integral, analytic continuation, program, or new measurement channel is used.

The two necessary existing objects are precisely the moment whole 10946 and the boxed whole 19788, whose author/peer sources are listed in section 9. Their already completed genuine whole consumption is reused. No new library search or old proof reprinting was performed.

## 3. Exact injectivity criterion over the integer kernel

Define the two K-valued responses of an added polynomial by

alpha(P) = <P,G> = D P(0),
beta(P)  = <P,xG> = D P(e_1).                                               (6)

For h = G(a+bx), finite linearity gives exactly

T_P(h) = a alpha(P) + b beta(P).                                            (7)

Consequently the augmented map (2) is injective if and only if

{(a,b) in Z^2 :
 a alpha(P_i) + b beta(P_i) = 0 for every i} = {(0,0)}.                       (8)

Proof: if (8) holds, the difference of two states with the same original seven readouts has the representation (3), and the added equalities force a=b=0. If (8) fails, choose a nonzero integer solution, form the actual signed array in (3), and take its nonnegative parts. Formula (4) gives a finite common mass and supplies a legal counterexample to (2).

For a single output, (8) says exactly that alpha(P) and beta(P) are linearly independent over Q. Indeed a rational relation becomes an integer one after clearing denominators, and every integer relation is a rational relation. This criterion uses independence over Q, not rank two over K. A single row always has rank at most one over K, but may be injective on the rank-two integer lattice.

For a finite family with rational coefficients, the response matrix has rational entries. In that case (8) is equivalent to its rank over Q being two: a rational null vector, when nonzero, can be cleared to a nonzero integer one.

This proves the new all-mass integer-kernel obligation explicitly.

## 4. A uniform degree obstruction, regardless of the number of outputs

Each forward difference in (5) lowers total polynomial degree by at least one, unless it gives zero. Hence D P has degree at most deg(P)-7.

If deg(P) <= 7, D P is a constant (possibly zero), so

alpha(P) = beta(P).                                                        (9)

Therefore any finite family whose members all have degree at most seven kills the same nonzero integer pair (a,b)=(1,-1). Its legal difference is

h = G(1-x), supported in the original B, with mu(1,-1)=126.                  (10)

Thus no such finite family satisfies (2), over any subfield K of R. Adding more degree-seven outputs does not repair the obstruction. This is stronger than observing that a particular degree-seven polynomial has a collision.

The obstruction does not contradict the old mass63 theorem. At mass63 its equality differences are different from (10). The new collision is a full-box, higher-mass difference whose existence is proved by the accepted integer kernel.

For the particular old degree-seven readout

P_7(u) = u_1^2 product_(j=2)^6 u_j,

the responses will be (2,2). In that case every unobserved nonzero difference is t G(1-x), t in Z \ {0}, and (4) gives common mass 126|t|. It follows that this fixed P_7 distinguishes every original fiber at masses M<126, and fails at every integer M>=126. For the latter assertion, start with h_+,h_- from (10) and add the same mass M-126 at any fixed voxel of B to both states. This last statement concerns exactly this P_7 and this fixed box.

## 5. Two explicit rational outputs of degree at most eight

Set

P_7(u) = u_1^2 product_(j=2)^6 u_j,
P_8(u) = u_1^3 product_(j=2)^6 u_j.                                        (11)

Their total degrees are seven and eight. Apply first the five differences in e_2,...,e_6. They remove the five linear factors in the remaining coordinates. The e_1 difference then gives, respectively,

2u_1+1,
3u_1^2+3u_1+1.

The final v difference shifts u_1 by one. Therefore the complete finite calculations are

D P_7(q) = 2,
D P_8(q) = 6(q_1+1).                                                       (12)

In particular,

(alpha(P_7), beta(P_7)) = (2,2),
(alpha(P_8), beta(P_8)) = (6,12).                                           (13)

The response matrix for the two outputs has determinant

2*12 - 2*6 = 12 != 0.                                                      (14)

Thus the two fixed rational (indeed integer-coefficient) polynomials P_7,P_8 satisfy (2), by (8).

Together with section 4, this proves that the minimum possible maximum degree of any finite rational-coefficient separating family is eight. It also gives an exact finite reconstruction of the boxed kernel coordinates from response differences: if r_7=2a+2b and r_8=6a+12b, then

b = r_8/6 - r_7/2,
a = r_7 - r_8/6.

These are algebraic identities for already integral a,b, not a claim of stable numerical inversion.

One rational-valued added polynomial cannot satisfy (2), at any degree. Its two responses are rational, and any two rational numbers have a nonzero integer relation. More explicitly, clear denominators so that alpha=A/q and beta=B/q with A,B integers. If (A,B)!=(0,0), let g=gcd(|A|,|B|); then the primitive relation is

(a_0,b_0)=(B/g,-A/g).                                                      (15)

It yields a nonzero legal collision by (3)-(4). If both responses vanish, (a,b)=(1,0) already gives such a collision. Consequently the minimum number of rational-valued polynomial outputs for (2) is two, and degree bound eight attains that minimum number.

For completeness, in the nonzero-response rational case all integer relations are multiples of (15). Hence the first possible collision mass is exactly mu(a_0,b_0); below it there is no collision, and at every mass at least that value there is one by adding common population. If both responses vanish, the first collision mass is 63. These exact statements use the same fixed family at all masses; they do not rule out a different rational design for a separately bounded population problem.

## 6. One exact irrational-field output, also with minimum degree eight

Suppose K is strictly larger than Q. Choose any eta in K \ Q and keep it fixed. The single polynomial

P_eta = P_7 + eta P_8                                                     (16)

has degree eight and lies in K[u]. Its response pair is

alpha(P_eta)=2+6eta,
beta(P_eta)=2+12eta.                                                        (17)

An integer relation between these responses reads

2(a+b) + 6eta(a+2b) = 0.

Since eta is irrational and both integer coefficients are rational, this forces a+b=0 and a+2b=0, hence a=b=0. Criterion (8) proves (2).

For example eta=sqrt(2) produces one exact Q(sqrt(2))-valued output. In that representation the output can be separated into its rational and sqrt(2) coefficients; it contains exactly the two rational linear measurements T_(P_7) and T_(P_8). The result counts field-valued outputs under the declared mathematical convention, not bits, physical sensors, or numerical effort.

Section 4 proves the sharp degree lower bound for this single-output construction: no polynomial of degree at most seven works, even with arbitrary real coefficients. No output at all works because the original box has the nonzero kernel G. Thus for K != Q the minimum number is one and the minimum degree of a single successful output is eight.

If K=Q, section 5 shows that no finite degree works for a single output. These alternatives exhaust the subfields K of R in the declared category.

## 7. Coordinate, positivity, and scope checks

All support statements remain in the original box B. The witness G(1-x) has X_1 degree at most three and all other coordinate degrees at most two, just as (3) requires. Its signed integer coefficients give genuine h_+,h_- in N_0^B, rather than a path in an auxiliary coefficient graph. Nonzero sign parts have the equal mass in (4).

The readout variable u is the integer coordinate of c+u in the given known chart, not an asserted integer physical coordinate c+u. Thus even if c has arbitrary real physical coordinates, evaluation of a K-coefficient polynomial at u stays in K. A different choice of origin in the same chart translates u by a known integer vector; rewriting the same readout in that coordinate system preserves K and total degree. The criterion (8) then uses the correspondingly translated finite pairing. This is covariance of the fixed known-chart formulation, not an extra family of physical observer axes.

For an explicit check of the forward-difference signs and shifts, (12) gives D P_7(0)=2 and D P_8(0)=6, while the xG generator uses e_1 and gives 2 and 12. Reversing the convention for the signed array reverses both observed responses together; the independence and collision statements are unchanged. The proof itself keeps the positive-shift convention in (5).

There is no passage from a polynomial spatial weight to a new native eighth coordinate. Every added T_P is explicitly an external mathematical readout of the existing finite state. There is no claim about two-long-axis boxes, arbitrary scale boxes, noise, approximate readouts, finite-precision realizability, or a Native program.

The rational obstruction is not a global impossibility for supplementary information: two rational outputs suffice, and a single exact irrational-field output also suffices. It concerns one rational polynomial output fixed uniformly across all masses on this box.

## 8. Bounded decision, coverage, and stop rule

The proposed discriminator was whether the two accepted interfaces supply a genuinely stronger all-mass readout statement, with coefficients and output fields fixed explicitly, or instead expose a type/quantifier mismatch.

The first outcome is proved here. The essential new step is the exact Z^2 response test (8), with legal nonnegative witnesses supplied by (3)-(4); degree-seven cancellation then acts on the actual pair of boxed generators. The rational/irrational distinction follows from this test and is classical linear algebra on the integer kernel. This is a RESULT_ONLY / COMPOSE appendix candidate for the existing readout family, not a new generic Tool or a separate paper claim.

Coverage was bounded to two already genuinely consumed wholes: 10946 supplies the fixed-polynomial/finite-difference category and its mass63 result; 19788 supplies the actual fixed-box all-mass integer kernel and mass formula. The earlier mass63 statement did not by itself state (8), did not include the h=G(1-x) higher-mass collision, and did not supply the declared field/output-count distinction. No all-library absence claim is made.

Kill conditions were: if only the old mass63 kappa test were recovered, record REUSE; if the boxed kernel were only real/rational instead of integer, or its support did not supply h_+,h_- in the actual B, retain HOLD; if any allowed readout/field changed the quantifiers, stop and restate the category before a conclusion. The literal integer kernel and finite pairing meet those conditions here. The bounded author exploration ends at this complete argument; no automatic palette, other-box, or parameter-variation branch is opened.
